newsitem.title: UK: UK natural gas slightly firmer, busy trade in Q4.
newsitem.headline: UK natural gas slightly firmer, busy trade in Q4.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices closed marginally up on Wednesday, although the change in levels was extremely modest, traders and dealers said.

The busiest period was Q4 97, which saw several deals done at both St Fergus and the NBP. And at least one player active in the NBP market said that it had been involved in a number of other Q4 trades on a private and confidential basis which were not reported.
"Q4 firmed up during the day and then softened," said a trader, who added that prices came down as some dealers looked for opportunities for profit taking at the end of the day.

One seller reported doing four deals at St Fergus in a hectic 30 minute spell in mid-morning. Two of the trades, for the January/February '98 strip at 16.60 pence and 16.70 pence, were seen by the market as being at unexpectedly high prices. And the seller added that the prices were the best he had yet done for this period.

"It indicates, even in the depth of the summer, the strength of Q1," he said. He added that as soon as the weather starts to turn cooler in September or October he expects the price to move higher quickly.

September 97 was also busy, with several trades done in a fairly tight range between 9.35 pence and 9.425 pence a therm. One dealer reported buying 50,000 th/d at 9.35 pence and then reselling it ten minutes later at 9.425 pence.

As usual there was also interest in the prompt period. Within day prices bounced right back up after trading down to 7.60 pence on Tuesday following a low flexibility mechanism system sell on Tuesday afternoon.
Prices of 9.60 pence and 9.65 pence were achieved, and a trader said these were still well below the system average price of around 11.50 pence.
Dealers said there were no headline news items driving prices and that Wednesday's market reflected pure trading activity and profit taking where possible.
